data.title: Coinbase Files With CFTC To List US Single-Stock Perpetual Futures, Including AAPL And TSLA Contracts
data.description:
Key points:
  • Coinbase Derivatives sought CFTC’s approval for perpetual futures on individual U.S. stocks.
  • Coinbase filed SEC notice registrations on September 1, making the CFTC request the second half of a two-regulator process.
  • Perpetual futures dominate global crypto trading but have never traded on a regulated U.S. venue, pushing American traders offshore.

Coinbase (COIN) Derivatives asked the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on Friday to approve perpetual futures on individual U.S. stocks, which would reportedly include Apple (AAPL) and Tesla (TSLA) contracts.

The filing urged the commission to approve "Equity Perpetual Contracts." Jane Downey, Coinbase Derivatives' chief regulatory officer, signed the letter, which explained the exchange intended to list the contracts "shortly following approval by the Commission, pending any additional necessary regulatory approvals."

The submission used an Apple contract as its representative specification, which was cash-settled, carried no fixed expiration, used hourly funding payments, and would trade from Sunday 8 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) to Friday 5 p.m. ET.

This is important because perpetual futures, or "perps," never expire. Traders can hold leveraged long or short positions indefinitely, and a periodic funding payment keeps the contract price tied to the underlying asset. The structure was built offshore on crypto rails, and U.S. traders have largely been locked out of it.

COIN stock closed in the green, up over 11% on Friday. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around COIN moved to the ‘neutral’ from the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Apple, Tesla In Lineup

The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported that Coinbase was the first company to file with the CFTC for U.S. single-stock perpetual futures. The Journal explained that Coinbase planned contracts on roughly 50 to 60 stocks, including Apple, Tesla, Microsoft (MSFT), and Nvidia (NVDA), with trading targeted for later this year. It further added that traders flocked to the offshore platform Hyperliquid (HYPE) for the same leveraged stock exposure.

On the same day, CEO Brian Armstrong also wrote on X that it was "time to bring stock perps onshore."

SEC Filings Came First

Friday's submission was only the second half of a two-regulator process. Because each contract references a single stock, it counts as a security futures product, which falls under both the CFTC and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Coinbase Derivatives filed a Form 1-N with the SEC on September 1 to register as a national securities exchange, and Coinbase Financial Markets filed a Form BD-N the same day as a security futures broker-dealer. Chief Policy Officer Faryar Shirzad announced the filings saying equity perps had "proven demand internationally" and that CFTC product approval was "the next step."

Tokenized Stocks Get Approval

The push landed days after the SEC approved a new "Innovation Exemption" on Thursday, allowing venues to trade tokenized U.S. stocks on blockchain for five years without registering as exchanges. The CFTC has not set a decision date on Coinbase's request.

data.title: SpiceJet flights delayed at Delhi Airport over 'operational' issues, leaving passengers stranded: What airline said
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 19 -- SpiceJet flights were delayed at Delhi Airport on Saturday, with the airline citing "operational reasons" for the disruption. The Indian low-cost carrier said that Leh- and Jammu-bound flights SG121 and SG127 arrived at their destinations.

The delays impacted hundreds of passengers who were stranded at the airport.

"On September 19, 2026, SpiceJet flights SG121 and SG127 operating from Delhi to Leh and SG2160 operating from Delhi to Jammu were delayed due to operational reasons. The flights have departed and already landed at their destinations. SpiceJet deeply regrets the inconvenience caused to the passengers," a SpiceJet spokesperson stated.

SpiceJet flight SG5111 from Delhi to Dubai, which was scheduled to leave Terminal 3 at 7.45 am, was also delayed. Flight-tracking data showed that the service eventually departed at 9.42 am.

The airline has been dealing with a prolonged financial crisis, leaving a large portion of its fleet grounded.

Delhi Airport authorities said that their ground teams were working closely with the airline and other stakeholders to assist passengers affected by the disruption.

"We regret the inconvenience faced by passengers due to the operational disruption of some SpiceJet flights. Delhi Airport teams are actively coordinating with the airline and relevant stakeholders to support affected passengers and provide necessary assistance to help," Delhi Airport wrote on X.

On September 15, two SpiceJet services from Delhi to Dubai, SG 5111 and SG 5105, were delayed for more than 24 hours after the aircraft were grounded, leading to protests by passengers at Delhi airport. Stranded travellers staged sit-ins and sought food, accommodation and regular updates from the airline.

Airport personnel later stepped in to assist the affected passengers. Some travellers also had confrontations with airport officials over restrictions on filming at the airport.

Meanwhile, SpiceJet said on September 3 that it was seeking funds under the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) as the airline continues to grapple with financial and operational challenges. Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu said that the government has also been urging the carrier to expand its operations.

Speaking to reporters, Naidu said the government maintains regular communication with airlines to understand their problems and has been in discussions with SpiceJet over its operational challenges, as per ANI.

"Every month, we engage with all the airlines regarding whatever difficulties or issues or challenges they have. SpiceJet also, in the same regard, we have been meeting," Naidu said.

He said the government has been encouraging SpiceJet to boost its operations, with particular emphasis on resolving its financial difficulties.

"And we have been pushing them to step up their operations, especially mainly the financial side of it. And they have also assured that they will be doing it quite soon," he mentioned.

Asked whether SpiceJet had approached the government for additional financial assistance, Naidu said the airline had not made such a request. He added, however, that the carrier was seeking financing through the ECLGS.

"No, in terms of support, there is the ECLGS scheme. They are trying to avail some money through that scheme," Naidu said. Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from MINT. data.title: ITC stock: 360 ONE maintains BUY, sees 65% upside; here's why brokerage is bullish
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 19 -- ITC is entering a crucial phase where the pressure on cigarette volumes is being weighed against improving realisations, a recovery in profitability and growth opportunities across its non-tobacco businesses. After a sharp decline over the past year, the stock is now being backed by 360 ONE Capital Research, which sees significant upside as these factors begin to reflect in earnings.

The brokerage has maintained its BUY rating on ITC with an unchanged target price of Rs.440 per share, compared with the current price of Rs.266. That implies a potential upside of around 68% from its previous close of Rs.262.20 per share on BSE.

"We continue to maintain BUY rating on the stock with a target price of Rs.440/share (unchanged), on a SOTP basis. Currently the stock trades at a P/E of 15.2x on FY28 basis," said 360 ONE Capital Research.

The stock has declined 36% over the past year and is trading close to its 52-week low of Rs.256. Meanwhile, it has shed 14% in 6 months, 10% in 3 months and 3% in the last 1 month.

360 ONE believes the recent weakness has created an opportunity as the impact of cigarette price increases starts flowing through profitability. At the same time, the brokerage expects support from FMCG, paperboards and packaging, agri and ITC's technology businesses.

"The stock has been range-bound in the last 2 months, driven by uncertainties related to the impact of the recent tax hikes on the overall cigarette volumes. However, we think, in the current industry dynamics, the pricing lever has more weight than the volumes lever, which should offset the decline in volumes that should follow, as the company has been raising pricing in well-known brands consistently in a staggered and phased manner," noted the brokerage.

The brokerage has made some changes to its earnings estimates, reflecting the sharper-than-expected impact of recent cigarette price increases on volumes.

"We have increased our volume degrowth assumption from -2.5% to -4% for FY27, driven by sharp price hikes done recently, resulting in a Revenue/EBITDA/PAT cut of -3%/-6%/-4%, while increasing our FY28 estimates a tad," it noted.

For the upcoming quarter, 360 ONE expects consolidated net revenue to fall 3.4% year-on-year, EBITDA to decline 10.3%, while PAT is expected to be 10.9% down.

The central argument behind the brokerage's positive stance is that pricing is becoming more important than volumes in the cigarette business. With ITC raising prices in a staggered manner across its brands, 360 ONE expects higher realisation to compensate for part of the volume decline.

The brokerage expects cigarette net realisation per stick to reach neutrality by Q4FY27 compared with Q3FY26. It also sees EBIT margins improving as successive price increases flow through the business.

The brokerage expects cigarette profitability to improve despite the volume pressure. ITC has already increased prices across key brands, with Classic Connect rising from Rs.19.5 to Rs.21.4 per stick and Gold Flake Superstar from Rs.7.9 to Rs.8.9.

"Current tax burden on cigarettes is ~65-67% of MRP, increasing from pre-tax hike figures of 53-54% and much closer to WHO recommendation of 75% of MRP (we rule out any sharp hike possibility in the coming years). With the last price increases, we estimate ~85% of ITC's portfolio has been covered in terms of net realisation per stick, pre tax increase levels. The benefit from lower-cost leaf tobacco inventory is expected to start reflecting from Q3FY27, approximating to Rs.10-15 paise/stick benefit," it added.

Beyond cigarettes, ITC's other businesses provide additional potential support. FMCG demand has remained healthy over the past six to nine months, helped by strong consumption and favourable macroeconomic conditions. Supply-chain disruptions affecting smaller competitors have also supported the segment. However, ITC has not yet fully passed on inflationary pressures, while higher fuel and crude prices could weigh on margins in the second half.

"As of the last 6-9 months FMCG demand remained healthy on account of good consumption demand, supported by better fundamental macroeconomic and supply-chain disruptions affecting smaller competitors. However, the company has not yet fully passed on the impact of inflation," said 360 ONE Capital Research.

Moreover, the paperboards, paper and packaging business is another area being watched. Integration of Century is expected from Q2FY27, taking combined paperboard capacity to around 1.5 million tonnes, from approximately 1 million tonnes earlier. The portfolio spans virgin board, recycled board and specialty products. Paperboard prices remain strong, while lower wood prices in North India are expected to provide a benefit from FY28.

ITC is also increasing its exposure to technology through the proposed Happiest Minds transaction. ITC Infotech will acquire a 22.1% promoter stake in Happiest Minds for Rs.13.3 billion, followed by a 25:81 share-swap merger. The combination will bring together Happiest Minds' AI, digital engineering, cloud and cybersecurity capabilities with ITC Infotech's enterprise technology services. ITC is expected to hold around 73.4% of the merged entity, with completion expected in approximately 15 months, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

Overall, 360 ONE's thesis is centred on improving profitability, a stronger FY28 earnings trajectory and increasing contributions from ITC's diversified businesses. With a Rs.440 target and a BUY recommendation, the brokerage expects the current weakness to give way to improved earnings visibility

data.title: Odisha Receives Rs 23,600 Cr Semiconductor Investment Proposals
data.description:
Proposals include SiC wafer, advanced packaging and semiconductor fabrication projects at various stages of review

Odisha has received investment proposals worth about Rs 23,600 crore for semiconductor projects, with the proposals at various stages of review, state officials said.

Among the proposals is one from QuadQuantum to establish a silicon carbide (SiC) substrate wafer facility in the state, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said while addressing media at Semicon India 2026.

The proposals are at various stages of review. The state is also in talks with Sancode Technologies over a second-phase advanced packaging facility, while SiCSem is exploring a combined SiC and gallium nitride (GaN) fab and packaging unit under a Phase-II expansion, and QuadQuantum is examining a raw material SiC wafers facility, Majhi said.

During the event, Majhi met semiconductor and technology companies, industry bodies, and delegations from Japan, Sweden and Taiwan. The companies included Lam Research, Applied Materials, SiCSem, 3D Glass Solutions, Cyient, Linde and Horiba India.

Separately, Odisha has five approved semiconductor manufacturing projects with a combined investment of Rs 10,899 crore, Majhi said. The projects cover SiC semiconductors, advanced packaging, glass substrate packaging, memory module assembly and power electronics. They are expected to create more than 4,500 direct jobs and over 16,000 indirect jobs.

SiCSem's integrated SiC fab and packaging facility and Heterogeneous Integration Packaging Solutions' (HIPS/3DGS) glass substrate packaging unit are among the 12 semiconductor projects approved nationally under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM).

Naraj Silicon Valley Plan

The state has also announced an 870-acre semiconductor and electronics hub at Naraj near Cuttack, to be called Odisha Silicon Valley. It is planned to house projects across semiconductors, electronics and information technology.

The site connects to the Cuttack-Bhubaneswar urban corridor and offers access to national highways and to the Paradip and Dhamra ports. The government also cites its proximity to the Mahanadi River as an advantage for industries with heavy water needs.

"The area for Odisha Silicon Valley in Naraj offers a highly favourable strategic location from the standpoint of connectivity and industrial infrastructure…Semiconductor fabrication facilities and assembly units require reliable access to substantial quantities of water and power, and the site's proximity to the Mahanadi River provides a significant locational advantage for meeting industrial water requirements," Majhi said.

The government is also citing the site’s proximity to the Mahanadi River as a factor for industries with substantial water requirements. “Semiconductor fabrication facilities and assembly units require reliable access to substantial quantities of water and power, and the site’s proximity to the Mahanadi River provides a significant locational advantage for meeting industrial water requirements. Combined with its connectivity and infrastructure potential, Naraj offers a strong foundation for developing a world-class semiconductor and electronics ecosystem,” he said.

“Naraj will be a potential strategic hub for the semiconductor supply chain, logistics and allied industries,” he said.

Fiscal Support

Odisha will provide an additional 25 per cent fiscal support on eligible capital expenditure (capex) for ISM-approved projects. The support covers semiconductor equipment manufacturing, semiconductor-grade chemicals, gases and materials, and other supply-chain segments. The state's policy also supports engineer relocation, workforce training, internships, international patent applications, and research and development.

The move follows the Centre's ISM 2.0 programme, which the Union Cabinet approved in July 2026 with an outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore.

"Our approach is to build the ecosystem around semiconductor investments, not look at projects in isolation," said Odisha Minister for Electronics & Information Technology Mukesh Mahaling. “Odisha has been an early mover in aligning its policy framework with ISM 2.0, while widening support to areas such as equipment, materials, gases and the supply chain.”

On project progress, RIR Power Electronics has completed erection and installation of reactors at its Bhubaneswar facility for SiC epitaxial wafer manufacturing, Majhi said. Commercial production at its integrated SiC facility is expected to begin soon.

The state is also in talks with Intel-3DGS to convert its memorandum of understanding into a proposed investment in advanced glass substrates and packaging. SiCSem is exploring a Phase-II expansion involving a combined SiC and gallium nitride (GaN) fab and packaging facility.

Odisha has also approved a Rs 452 crore National Industry Co-Development Hub on Integrated Power Electronics at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bhubaneswar under the Indian Design, Semiconductors, Packaging and Systems programme.

data.title: Aye Finance Appoints Nishit Shrivastava As Chief Technology Officer
data.description:
Shrivastava joins from Muthoot Fincorp with over 24 years of experience to lead technology strategy and digital transformation at Aye Finance

Aye Finance has appointed Nishit Shrivastava as Chief Technology Officer (CTO), as the non-banking financial company looks to strengthen its technology capabilities and scale lending operations across India’s micro-enterprise segment.

Shrivastava brings more than 24 years of experience in software development and financial services technology, spanning fintech, digital transformation, technology strategy and enterprise platforms. He most recently served as Chief Information and Technology Officer at Muthoot Fincorp, part of the Muthoot Pappachan Group.

At Muthoot Fincorp, he led technology initiatives across customer experience, data engineering, modern infrastructure, digital transformation, security, technology resilience and enterprise artificial intelligence. His experience includes developing and managing technology capabilities within financial services businesses.

At Aye Finance, Shrivastava will lead the company’s technology strategy, focusing on strengthening its architecture and building scalable, secure and resilient digital platforms. His mandate will also include using data, AI and emerging technologies to enhance technology-enabled lending, improve operational efficiency and support customer experience.

Sanjay Sharma, Managing Director, Aye Finance, said technology has been central to the company’s lending model and will become increasingly important as it enters its next phase of growth. He said Shrivastava’s experience in financial services technology and enterprise-scale transformation would support the company’s efforts to improve efficiency and customer value.

Shrivastava said he would focus on building technology capabilities that can scale with the business, strengthen data-led decision-making and help make credit more accessible and responsive for micro-enterprises.

data.title: Leadership Is Not About Avoiding Hard Choices: Biocon's CHRO On Making The Layoff Call
data.description:
Naveen Narayanan on the four questions he asks himself before every layoff, restructuring or termination, and why dignity in execution matters as much as the decision itself

Naveen Narayanan, CHRO of Biocon, doesn't reach for the usual HR hedges. Across this conversation, he argues that AI will genuinely eliminate some jobs even as it creates others, closing the leadership gender gap needs "equity at home" as much as workplace policy, burnout is really a failure of purpose and psychological safety rather than pressure itself, and ESG has no business sitting outside the P&L. He also takes on the harder institutional questions — whether HR is built for advocacy or liability, whether "one culture" survives across dozens of geographies, and how he personally sits with a layoff decision.

Excerpts:

Most companies now say some version of "AI won't replace jobs, it'll change them." How much of that is genuinely true, and how much is HR softening a harder conversation that leadership isn't ready to have with employees yet?

The statement is directionally true, but it's not the complete truth. AI will eliminate tasks, redefine roles and, in certain cases, reduce the need for certain jobs. Leaders should be honest about each of these scenarios with their people. But focusing only on job displacement misses the larger story. Most jobs are a combination of judgment, expertise, collaboration and human connection. AI will change that mix—automating some tasks, augmenting others and making new capabilities more valuable. Some industries are surely getting disrupted and certain others augmented.

The responsibility of leaders and HR is not to soften the conversation, but to make it honest and actionable. Employees deserve clarity about what is changing, what skills will be needed in the future, and how the organisation will support their transition. The real question is not “Which jobs will AI replace?” but “How do we help our people evolve their capabilities to create greater value in an AI-enabled workplace?”. I have always believed that the person who knows how to work with AI will replace the person who doesn’t know AI. That requires AI literacy, fluency, alongside judgment, creativity, empathy, resilience and collaboration.

Every senior HR leader eventually has to make or defend a call - a layoff, a termination, a restructuring - that no policy document fully justifies. How do you personally sit with decisions like that without either becoming numb to them or letting them paralyse you?

As a CHRO, I am equally an enterprise leader as much as the leader of the function. I don’t need anyone to tell me on a layoff due to economic circumstances or other reasons as I am equally part of running a business.  These decisions however are never easy and should be the last resort. And most important is how respectfully are these carried out. I tend to work through four questions: Is the decision necessary? Have we genuinely considered alternatives? Is it fair and consistent? And can we implement it with dignity?

The first two ensure we are solving a real business need rather than taking the easiest route. The third tests whether the decision is being applied objectively, without compromising our values. The fourth reminds us that behind every organisational decision are people whose lives may be significantly affected. Companies ensure generous packages, outplacement services, some even do job fairs, counselling for employees and family to ensure their colleagues land on their feet. People appreciate honesty and clarity in such situations. The measure of leadership is not avoiding difficult choices but making them responsibly and standing behind them with integrity.

Entry-level diversity numbers have improved industry wide. But representation still tends to thin out sharply the higher you go. Why do you think that pattern persists almost everywhere, despite how much has been invested in fixing it?

I think the pattern persists because representation at senior levels is shaped by many factors accumulated over a career—not simply by hiring. As careers progress, the talent pool of women becomes narrower due to many life situations. A radical thought out there is to assess women for their potential compared to others as there is always a time gap for many. Leadership roles demand experience, business exposure and the ability to navigate increasing complexity and these come through many life events. The pathways through which people build these experiences are influenced by many factors, including individual choices, circumstances and career decisions.

So, while entry-level representation has improved, we need a lot more social change and push, equity at home to translate a larger talent pool availability into senior leadership representation. Biocon has achieved 20 per cent representation in the mid and senior leadership, starting from the CXO team. Several parts of our business such as the Malaysia plant and our scientific verticals are close to being gender equal.

"High-performance culture" is a phrase almost every company uses, and it's also one of the most common precursors to burnout. Where do you draw the line between pushing performance and quietly damaging the people delivering it?

I don't see performance and wellbeing as opposing priorities. A high-performance culture should enable both. Some roles are inherently high-pressure, and that reality needs to be acknowledged by the individuals who have chosen that path. It is important to assess not just technical capability, but also a person's maturity, resilience and ability to operate effectively under sustained pressure. Burn-out occurs when people stop having fun in their work, lack direction or purpose and most importantly psychological safety. Why do entrepreneurs not burn out? Because they have created this for themselves in a high performing environment.

The distinction should be between periods of intensity vs a culture of unnecessary excessive pressure where the latter is difficult to sustain. For me, high performance requires clarity on purpose and priorities, clear expectations, strong managers and an environment where people can speak openly when demands become unsustainable. The measure of a high-performance culture is not how much pressure people can absorb, but whether the organisation enables them to perform consistently and sustainably. Biocon has always been purpose driven, hundreds of our colleagues have spent 2 or 3 decades in the firm. The enthusiasm is fuelled because of the nurturing environment.

ESG commitments sound clean in a mission statement but get complicated the moment they collide with a quarterly target or a cost pressure. When that collision actually happens inside a company, what usually wins - and what should win?

Sustainability of business outcomes is not an agenda outside of business – quarter or annual. We confuse ESG with environment or social indicators. I don't think ESG should sit outside the business, competing with commercial priorities. If it does, you have the wrong agenda. For example – ESG includes strength of succession pipeline, strength of governance and many such aspects. Today to win commercial contracts in many parts of the world, ESG scores are not only a gating criterion but also a differentiator as we have seen.

The better approach is to build ESG considerations into the operating fabric of the organization and how decisions are made—from capital allocation and operations to leadership KPIs and how we develop people and engage communities. There will be situations where short-term financial pressures can delay or create difficult choices. The question then is whether we are optimising for the next month or quarter or protecting the organisation's ability to create value over the longer term.

For me, what should win is the decision that is responsible for the business and its sustainability over the long term. Investments can happen in one quarter or another towards this. Biocon has made significant strides to be in the top quartile of many ESG ratings. Off late, we have even won certain tenders' basis the ESG achievements which actually shows that it can be a competitive advantage.

When an organisation operates across dozens of geographies, "one culture" is often more slogan than reality. What, in your view, is actually consistent - and what has to be allowed to differ by region without the whole thing falling apart?

We mix culture as a term with ways of working. I prefer the latter. Do organisations have one way to make decisions, take risks, deal with people and so on? If yes, then you have a unified culture. Some people or geographies may be additive to the ways of working/culture and some maybe dilutive but that is more an implementation and execution issue. You can have this situation in the same building under two different leaders.

Global organisations are also tied by a common purpose and that’s a larger unifying force guiding ways of working. What will not differ are core values that define who we are—integrity, respect for people, ethical conduct, accountability and our commitment to the organisation's purpose. These are non-negotiable, irrespective of geography. How these get expressed, can reflect local realities.

Leadership styles, communication, workplace practices and approaches to engagement can differ across markets. Localisation is very important because employees will connect with it when they see it reflected in their context. Strong global cultures are not built by making every market identical; they are built by being clear about what is non-negotiable while giving local teams the freedom to make it relevant to their context.
